podcast.body: This song served as the lead single from *The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars* and was David Bowie's first hit since "Space Oddity" in 1969. Its success earned Bowie a performance spot on Top of the Pops, where he appeared with short-cropped hair and a multicolored jumpsuit, famously flirting with guitarist Mick Ronson and shocking parents while thrilling young audiences. The lyrics are written from the perspective of someone listening to Ziggy on the radio, hearing "hazy cosmic jive." "Here's a Starman. Waking up the sky."

podcast.body: This song was released as a single from the "Ziggy Stardust" album in 1972. Its B-side was "Suffragette City." "When David Bowie really starman as a single from the Ziggy Stardust album in 1972, the B side, the extra after the fact song, was this."

podcast.body: This song, released in conjunction with 'The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and The Spiders from Mars' LP, made the singles top 10 in the UK. It was a key track in Bowie's image-making breakthrough, solidifying his orange-haired glam rock alien alter ego, Ziggy Stardust, in the public consciousness. "In the UK, the album cracked the top 10, and the song Starman made the singles top 10 as well."
